questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Gulmarg, one of the most famous tourist destinations in J&K, is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Gulmarg is located in Baramulla district of J&K, at an altitude of about 2,650 m. Srinagar is wrong — it is a separate district; Anantnag is wrong — Pahalgam is in Anantnag; Budgam is wrong — it lies between Srinagar and Gulmarg but Gulmarg falls in Baramulla.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Pahalgam:

(i) It is known as the 'Valley of Shepherds'.
(ii) It serves as the base camp for the Amarnath Yatra.
(iii) The Lidder River flows through Pahalgam.
(iv) It is located in Baramulla district.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Pahalgam means 'Valley of Shepherds' (i-correct), it is the traditional base camp for Amarnath Yatra (ii-correct), and the Lidder River flows through it (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because Pahalgam is located in Anantnag district, not Baramulla.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The famous Mughal Garden 'Shalimar Bagh' in Srinagar was built by:
questions.explanation: Shalimar Bagh was built by Mughal Emperor Jahangir in 1619 for his wife Nur Jahan. Akbar is wrong — he did not build gardens in Kashmir; Shah Jahan is wrong — he later extended it but did not build it; Aurangzeb is wrong — he had no association with this garden's construction.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Dal Lake is one of the most visited tourist attractions in J&K.
Reason (R): Dal Lake offers unique houseboat stays, shikara rides, and floating markets that attract tourists from around the world.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Dal Lake is indeed one of J&K's most popular tourist spots (A is correct). The houseboats, shikara rides, and floating markets are the key attractions that make it so popular (R is correct and directly explains A). Option 2 is wrong because R specifically explains why Dal Lake is popular; Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct; Option 4 is wrong because A is also correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are famous Mughal Gardens in Srinagar?

(i) Shalimar Bagh
(ii) Nishat Bagh
(iii) Chasma Shahi
(iv) Tulip Garden

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Shalimar Bagh (built by Jahangir), Nishat Bagh (built by Asif Khan), and Chasma Shahi (built by Shah Jahan) are all Mughal Gardens (i, ii, iii correct). The Tulip Garden (iv) is wrong because it is the Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden, a modern garden opened in 2007, not a Mughal-era garden.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Sonamarg, meaning 'Meadow of Gold', is located on the route to:
questions.explanation: Sonamarg lies on the Srinagar-Leh highway and is the last major town before the Zoji La Pass on the way to Ladakh/Leh. Gulmarg is wrong — it is in a different direction (Baramulla side); Pahalgam is wrong — it is in Anantnag direction; Kishtwar is wrong — it is in a completely different region of J&K.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following tourist destinations with their popular names:

Column I:
(a) Gulmarg
(b) Pahalgam
(c) Sonamarg
(d) Srinagar

Column II:
(i) Venice of the East
(ii) Meadow of Gold
(iii) Meadow of Flowers
(iv) Valley of Shepherds

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Gulmarg means 'Meadow of Flowers' (a-iii); Pahalgam means 'Valley of Shepherds' (b-iv); Sonamarg means 'Meadow of Gold' (c-ii); Srinagar is called 'Venice of the East' (d-i). Option 2 incorrectly assigns 'Valley of Shepherds' to Gulmarg; Option 3 swaps Pahalgam and Sonamarg meanings; Option 4 assigns 'Meadow of Gold' to Gulmarg.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Gulmarg Gondola is famous for being one of the highest cable car systems in the world. Its second phase takes tourists up to which peak?
questions.explanation: The Gulmarg Gondola Phase 2 takes visitors to Apharwat Peak at about 4,200 m altitude. Pir Panjal Peak is wrong — it is a mountain range, not the gondola destination; Kolahoi Peak is wrong — it is near Pahalgam; Haramukh Peak is wrong — it is in Ganderbal district.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Amarnath Cave:

(i) It is located at an altitude of approximately 3,888 m.
(ii) It houses a naturally formed ice Shiva Lingam.
(iii) The annual Amarnath Yatra takes place during July-August.
(iv) The cave is located in Srinagar district.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Amarnath Cave is at approx. 3,888 m (i-correct), contains a natural ice Shiva Lingam (ii-correct), and the yatra occurs in July-August (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because the cave is located in Anantnag district, not Srinagar.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden, Asia's largest tulip garden, is located on the foothills of which mountain range?
questions.explanation: The Tulip Garden is located on the foothills of the Zabarwan Range, overlooking Dal Lake in Srinagar. Pir Panjal Range is wrong — it separates the Kashmir Valley from Jammu; Karakoram Range is wrong — it is in Ladakh; Shivalik Range is wrong — it is in the Jammu region.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Gulmarg is a major skiing destination in India during winter.
Reason (R): Gulmarg receives heavy snowfall and has slopes suitable for skiing at an altitude of about 2,650 m.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Gulmarg is India's premier skiing destination (A is correct). Its high altitude, heavy snowfall, and suitable slopes make it ideal for skiing (R is correct and directly explains A). Option 2 is wrong because R precisely explains why Gulmarg is a ski destination; Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct; Option 4 is wrong because A is also correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Nishat Bagh ('Garden of Joy') in Srinagar was built by:
questions.explanation: Nishat Bagh was built by Asif Khan (brother of Empress Nur Jahan and father-in-law of Shah Jahan) in 1633. Nur Jahan is wrong — Shalimar Bagh was built for her; Emperor Jahangir is wrong — he built Shalimar Bagh; Shah Jahan is wrong — he built Chasma Shahi.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following tourist spots are located in the Anantnag district of J&K?

(i) Pahalgam
(ii) Kokernag Spring
(iii) Verinag
(iv) Gulmarg

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Pahalgam (i-correct), Kokernag Spring (ii-correct), and Verinag (iii-correct — source of Jhelum River) are all in Anantnag district. Statement (iv) is wrong because Gulmarg is in Baramulla district, not Anantnag.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Vaishno Devi shrine, one of India's most visited religious tourist destinations, is located in which district of J&K?
questions.explanation: Vaishno Devi shrine is located in the Trikuta Mountains of Reasi district (formerly part of Udhampur). Jammu is wrong — it is the nearest major city but not the district; Udhampur is wrong — the shrine was transferred to Reasi when the district was carved out; Kathua is wrong — it is a different district in the Jammu region.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Patnitop:

(i) It is a hill station located in Udhampur district.
(ii) It is situated at an altitude of approximately 2,024 m.
(iii) It lies on the Jammu-Srinagar National Highway.
(iv) It is famous for its hot sulphur springs.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Patnitop is in Udhampur district (i-correct), at about 2,024 m altitude (ii-correct), and lies on the Jammu-Srinagar NH (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because Patnitop is not known for hot sulphur springs — that description fits places like Tattapani in Rajouri.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Shankaracharya Temple in Srinagar is situated on top of __________ Hill and offers panoramic views of the Kashmir Valley.
questions.explanation: The Shankaracharya Temple sits atop Takht-e-Sulaiman (Throne of Solomon) Hill at about 1,000 feet above the valley floor. Hari Parbat is wrong — it is a separate hill with a fort in Srinagar; Zabarwan is wrong — it is a mountain range; Mahadev is wrong — it is not the name of this hill.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following tourist spots with the districts they are located in:

Column I:
(a) Vaishno Devi
(b) Patnitop
(c) Gulmarg
(d) Pahalgam

Column II:
(i) Anantnag
(ii) Baramulla
(iii) Reasi
(iv) Udhampur

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Vaishno Devi is in Reasi (a-iii); Patnitop is in Udhampur (b-iv); Gulmarg is in Baramulla (c-ii); Pahalgam is in Anantnag (d-i). Option 2 swaps Reasi and Udhampur; Option 3 swaps Gulmarg and Pahalgam districts; Option 4 wrongly places Patnitop in Baramulla.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Betaab Valley near Pahalgam derives its name from:
options: A historical battle fought at the site
The shape of the valley resembling a heart
questions.explanation: Betaab Valley was named after the 1983 Bollywood movie 'Betaab' (starring Sunny Deol) which was extensively shot there. A folk legend is wrong — no such legend exists; a historical battle is wrong — no battle occurred here; the valley shape is wrong — the name has no connection to geography.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Hari Parbat Fort in Srinagar:

(i) It is built on a hill overlooking Dal Lake.
(ii) It was originally fortified during the Mughal period.
(iii) The fort was later strengthened by Afghan governors.
(iv) It is located in Baramulla district.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Hari Parbat Fort overlooks Dal Lake (i-correct), was built during the Mughal period by Emperor Akbar (ii-correct), and was later strengthened by Afghan governors (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because the fort is in Srinagar district, not Baramulla.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Bahu Fort in Jammu is situated on the banks of which river?
questions.explanation: Bahu Fort, one of the oldest structures in Jammu, is located on the left bank of the River Tawi. Chenab is wrong — it flows through Doda and Kishtwar; Jhelum is wrong — it flows through the Kashmir Valley; Ravi is wrong — it flows along the border near Kathua.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Houseboats on Dal Lake are a unique tourist attraction not commonly found elsewhere in India.
Reason (R): The tradition of houseboats in Kashmir began during the British colonial period when outsiders were not allowed to own land in the region.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Houseboats are indeed unique to Kashmir tourism in India (A is correct). The British built houseboats because the Maharaja's law prohibited non-Kashmiris from owning land, so they created floating homes (R is correct and explains why this tradition developed). Option 2 is wrong because R directly explains the origin of A; Option 3 is wrong because R is historically accurate; Option 4 is wrong because A is factually correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Martand Sun Temple, an ancient Hindu temple ruin, is located near which town in J&K?
questions.explanation: The Martand Sun Temple ruins are located near Mattan in Anantnag district, built by King Lalitaditya Muktapida in the 8th century. Srinagar is wrong — no Sun Temple ruins exist there; Jammu is wrong — it is in a different region; Pattan is wrong — it is in Baramulla district.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are popular trekking destinations in J&K?

(i) Tarsar-Marsar Lake trek
(ii) Great Lakes trek (Kashmir)
(iii) Kolahoi Glacier trek
(iv) Rohtang Pass trek

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Tarsar-Marsar Lakes (i-correct), Great Lakes of Kashmir (ii-correct), and Kolahoi Glacier near Pahalgam (iii-correct) are all popular J&K treks. Statement (iv) is wrong because Rohtang Pass is in Himachal Pradesh, not in J&K.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Hazratbal Shrine in Srinagar is famous because it:
options: Contains the tomb of Sheikh Abdullah
Houses a relic believed to be of Prophet Muhammad
Is the oldest mosque in Kashmir
questions.correctAnswer: Houses a relic believed to be of Prophet Muhammad
questions.explanation: Hazratbal Shrine is revered as it houses the Moi-e-Muqaddas (sacred relic believed to be a hair of Prophet Muhammad). The tomb of Sheikh Abdullah is wrong — he is buried at his own mausoleum; built by Akbar is wrong — it was built later; oldest mosque is wrong — that distinction belongs to other mosques in Kashmir.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Yusmarg:

(i) It is located in Budgam district.
(ii) It is known as the 'Meadow of Jesus'.
(iii) It is surrounded by dense pine forests.
(iv) It is the base camp for Amarnath Yatra.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Yusmarg is in Budgam district (i-correct), its name means 'Meadow of Jesus' (ii-correct), and it is surrounded by pine and fir forests (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because Pahalgam and Baltal are the base camps for Amarnath Yatra, not Yusmarg.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Dachigam National Park near Srinagar is primarily famous for the conservation of:
questions.explanation: Dachigam is the last remaining home of the Hangul (Kashmir Stag), an endangered species. Snow Leopard is wrong — they are found at much higher altitudes in Ladakh; Himalayan Black Bear is wrong — while present, it's not the primary conservation focus; Markhor is wrong — it is found in other regions.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Mughal Road is being developed as an alternative route connecting Kashmir Valley to Jammu.
Reason (R): The existing Jammu-Srinagar National Highway through Jawahar Tunnel frequently gets blocked due to landslides and heavy snowfall.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The Mughal Road (Bafliaz to Shopian) is being developed as an alternative route (A is correct). The frequent closure of the Jammu-Srinagar NH due to natural disasters necessitates an alternative (R is correct and explains A). Option 2 is wrong because R directly explains the need for the Mughal Road; Option 3 is wrong because R is factually accurate; Option 4 is wrong because A is also correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following religious tourist destinations with their significance:

Column I:
(a) Vaishno Devi
(b) Amarnath Cave
(c) Hazratbal Shrine
(d) Charar-e-Sharief

Column II:
(i) Shrine of Sheikh Noor-ud-din Noorani (Nund Rishi)
(ii) Ice Shiva Lingam
(iii) Sacred relic (Moi-e-Muqaddas)
(iv) Hindu goddess shrine in Trikuta Mountains

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Vaishno Devi is a Hindu goddess shrine in Trikuta Mountains (a-iv); Amarnath has the ice Shiva Lingam (b-ii); Hazratbal houses the Moi-e-Muqaddas (c-iii); Charar-e-Sharief is the shrine of Nund Rishi (d-i). Option 2 swaps Amarnath and Hazratbal; Option 3 swaps Vaishno Devi and Amarnath; Option 4 swaps Hazratbal and Charar-e-Sharief.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The famous Shikara boats are primarily associated with which water body in J&K?
questions.explanation: Shikara boats are iconic to Dal Lake in Srinagar, used for transportation, tourism, and the floating vegetable market. Wular Lake is wrong — it is used mainly for fishing; Manasbal Lake is wrong — shikaras are rare there; Pangong Lake is wrong — it is in Ladakh and too remote for shikaras.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Hemis Monastery:

(i) It is the largest and wealthiest monastery in Ladakh.
(ii) It belongs to the Drukpa Kagyu lineage of Buddhism.
(iii) The annual Hemis Festival celebrates the birth of Guru Padmasambhava.
(iv) It is located in the Kashmir Valley near Srinagar.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Hemis is the largest monastery in Ladakh (i-correct), belongs to Drukpa Kagyu lineage (ii-correct), and the festival celebrates Guru Padmasambhava's birth anniversary (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because Hemis is in Leh district of Ladakh, not in the Kashmir Valley.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Amar Mahal Palace Museum in Jammu was built in the style of:
questions.explanation: Amar Mahal Palace was built in the 19th century in the style of a French chateau for Raja Amar Singh. Mughal architecture is wrong — the palace is not Mughal-style; Rajput architecture is wrong — it does not follow Rajput design; British colonial is wrong — it was specifically designed in French style.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are popular tourist destinations in the Jammu region?

(i) Patnitop
(ii) Bhaderwah
(iii) Kishtwar
(iv) Sonamarg

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Patnitop (hill station, i-correct), Bhaderwah ('Mini Kashmir', ii-correct), and Kishtwar (scenic valley, iii-correct) are all in the Jammu region. Statement (iv) is wrong because Sonamarg is in the Kashmir Valley (Ganderbal district), not in the Jammu region.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Manasbal Lake is famous for its lotus blooms and is known as the:
options: Supreme Gem of All Kashmir Lakes
questions.correctAnswer: Supreme Gem of All Kashmir Lakes
questions.explanation: Manasbal Lake has been described as the 'Supreme Gem of All Kashmir Lakes' due to its unmatched scenic beauty. 'Jewel of Kashmir's Lakes' is wrong — not an established name; 'Pearl of the Valley' is wrong — this is not the recognized title; 'Crown of Kashmir Waters' is wrong — not a known appellation.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Bhaderwah:

(i) It is often called 'Mini Kashmir' or 'Chota Kashmir'.
(ii) It is located in Doda district.
(iii) It is surrounded by snow-covered mountains and lush green meadows.
(iv) It is located in the Kashmir Valley.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Bhaderwah is called 'Mini Kashmir' (i-correct), is in Doda district (ii-correct), and is surrounded by scenic mountains and meadows (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because Bhaderwah is in the Jammu division, not in the Kashmir Valley.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Pari Mahal ('Palace of Fairies') in Srinagar was built by:
questions.explanation: Pari Mahal was built by Prince Dara Shikoh (son of Shah Jahan) as a library and learning centre. Emperor Jahangir is wrong — he built Shalimar Bagh; Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin is wrong — he ruled in the 15th century, before Mughal influence; Maharaja Gulab Singh is wrong — he came in the 19th century.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Ladakh has become a popular adventure tourism destination in recent years.
Reason (R): Ladakh offers opportunities for mountaineering, river rafting on the Zanskar and Indus rivers, and motorcycle touring on high-altitude roads.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Ladakh has become a major adventure tourism hub (A is correct). Its mountaineering, rafting, and motorcycle touring opportunities directly explain why it attracts adventure tourists (R is correct and explains A). Option 2 is wrong because R directly explains A; Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct; Option 4 is wrong because A is also correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The famous floating vegetable market ('Raadh') on Dal Lake operates during:
questions.explanation: The floating vegetable market on Dal Lake operates in the early morning hours (around 5-6 AM, before sunrise). Afternoon is wrong — the market is closed by then; evening is wrong — no trading occurs; late night is wrong — the market starts at dawn.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Verinag:

(i) It is believed to be the source of the River Jhelum.
(ii) It has an octagonal spring built by Emperor Jahangir.
(iii) It is located in Anantnag district.
(iv) It is primarily known as a skiing destination.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Verinag is believed to be the source of the Jhelum (i-correct), has a Mughal-built octagonal basin around the spring (ii-correct), and is in Anantnag district (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because Verinag is a spring/garden site, not a skiing destination — skiing is done in Gulmarg.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following tourist sites with their key attractions:

Column I:
(a) Dachigam National Park
(b) Betaab Valley
(c) Manasbal Lake
(d) Shankaracharya Temple

Column II:
(i) Lotus blooms and bird watching
(ii) Ancient Hindu temple on hilltop
(iii) Bollywood shooting location near Pahalgam
(iv) Hangul deer conservation

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Dachigam is known for Hangul conservation (a-iv); Betaab Valley for Bollywood film shooting (b-iii); Manasbal for lotus and bird watching (c-i); Shankaracharya is an ancient hilltop temple (d-ii). Option 2 wrongly assigns lotus to Betaab Valley; Option 3 swaps Dachigam and Betaab; Option 4 swaps Manasbal and Shankaracharya features.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Gurez Valley, a scenic tourist destination close to the Line of Control, is accessible through:
questions.explanation: Gurez Valley is accessible through the Razdan Pass from Bandipora district. Zoji La Pass is wrong — it leads to Ladakh from Sonamarg; Banihal Pass is wrong — it connects Jammu to Kashmir Valley; Pir Panjal Pass is wrong — it is a general mountain range pass south of the valley.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the approximate altitude (in metres) of popular tourist destinations in J&K:

| Destination | Altitude (m) |
|------------|-------------|
| Gulmarg | 2,650 |
| Pahalgam | 2,130 |
| Sonamarg | 2,740 |
| Patnitop | 2,024 |
| Srinagar | 1,585 |

Which destination has the highest altitude?
questions.explanation: From the data, Sonamarg has the highest altitude at 2,740 m. Gulmarg is wrong (2,650 m — second highest); Pahalgam is wrong (2,130 m); Patnitop is wrong (2,024 m).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Kokernag Spring in Anantnag is the largest freshwater spring in J&K and feeds into which river?
questions.explanation: Kokernag Spring feeds into the Bringi Nallah (stream), which eventually joins the Jhelum. Jhelum is wrong — the spring doesn't directly feed the Jhelum; Lidder is wrong — it flows through Pahalgam; Chenab is wrong — it flows through Doda/Kishtwar, far from Kokernag.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Aru Valley:

(i) It is located near Pahalgam in Anantnag district.
(ii) It is a popular base camp for trekking to Kolahoi Glacier.
(iii) It is known for its meadows, forests, and adventure tourism.
(iv) It is famous for its ancient Buddhist monastery.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Aru Valley is near Pahalgam (i-correct), serves as base for Kolahoi Glacier trek (ii-correct), and is known for meadows and adventure tourism (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because Aru Valley has no Buddhist monastery — monasteries are primarily in Ladakh.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following lakes are popular tourist attractions in the Kashmir region?

(i) Dal Lake
(ii) Nigeen Lake
(iii) Manasbal Lake
(iv) Tso Moriri

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Dal Lake, Nigeen Lake (Srinagar), and Manasbal Lake (Ganderbal) are all popular Kashmir tourist spots (i, ii, iii correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because Tso Moriri is located in Ladakh (Changthang plateau), not in the Kashmir region.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Raghunath Temple in Jammu is one of the largest temple complexes in North India. It was built by:
questions.explanation: The Raghunath Temple was started by Maharaja Gulab Singh but completed by his son Maharaja Ranbir Singh in 1860. While Gulab Singh initiated it, Ranbir Singh is credited with completing it. Pratap Singh is wrong — he came later; Hari Singh is wrong — he was the last Dogra ruler.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Baltal route and the __________ route are the two traditional paths for the Amarnath Yatra pilgrimage.
questions.explanation: The two traditional routes for Amarnath Yatra are the Pahalgam route (longer, traditional) and the Baltal route (shorter, steeper). Sonamarg is wrong — it is near Baltal but not the named route; Gulmarg is wrong — it has no connection to Amarnath Yatra; Yusmarg is wrong — it is in Budgam with no Amarnath route.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Srinagar is called the 'Venice of the East'.
Reason (R): Srinagar has numerous lakes, waterways, and canals similar to Venice, with transportation via boats (shikaras) on its water channels.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Srinagar is indeed called 'Venice of the East' (A is correct). Its network of lakes, waterways, and boat-based transport resembles Venice, explaining the name (R is correct and explains A). Option 2 is wrong because the water features directly explain the Venice comparison; Option 3 is wrong because R is factually accurate; Option 4 is wrong because A is also correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows annual tourist arrivals (in lakhs) to J&K over five years:

| Year | Tourist Arrivals (Lakhs) |
|------|-------------------------|
| 2017 | 135 |
| 2018 | 160 |
| 2019 | 90 |
| 2020 | 35 |
| 2021 | 110 |

In which year was the percentage decline (compared to the previous year) the greatest?
questions.explanation: Percentage decline in 2019 = (160−90)/160 × 100 = 43.75%. Percentage decline in 2020 = (90−35)/90 × 100 = 61.1%. 2020 shows the greatest percentage decline at 61.1%. 2018 is wrong — it saw an increase, not decline; 2019 is wrong — its decline was 43.75%, less than 2020's 61.1%; 2021 is wrong — it saw an increase from 35 to 110 lakhs.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Mughal Gardens of Kashmir:

(i) They are designed in the Persian 'Charbagh' (four-part) style.
(ii) They feature terraced lawns, flowing water channels, and fountains.
(iii) All three major Mughal Gardens in Srinagar are on the banks of Wular Lake.
(iv) They were built during the 16th-17th centuries.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Mughal Gardens follow the Charbagh style (i-correct), feature terraces, water channels and fountains (ii-correct), and were built in the 16th-17th centuries (iv-correct). Statement (iii) is wrong because the major gardens (Shalimar, Nishat, Chasma Shahi) are on the banks of Dal Lake, not Wular Lake.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following hill stations with their popular descriptive names:

Column I:
(a) Bhaderwah
(b) Gulmarg
(c) Yusmarg
(d) Sanasar

Column II:
(i) Meadow of Jesus
(ii) Mini Kashmir
(iii) Mini Switzerland of J&K
(iv) Meadow of Flowers

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Bhaderwah is called 'Mini Kashmir' (a-ii); Gulmarg means 'Meadow of Flowers' (b-iv); Yusmarg means 'Meadow of Jesus' (c-i); Sanasar is called 'Mini Switzerland of J&K' (d-iii). Option 2 swaps Bhaderwah and Gulmarg; Option 3 swaps Yusmarg and Sanasar; Option 4 wrongly assigns 'Meadow of Jesus' to Gulmarg.
